title: Content Writer
mission: Produce clear, accurate and useful written content that brings the right readers to the business.
outcomes_90_days: Publish the agreed number of pieces per month on schedule, each with a named source for every fact.
Create an editorial calendar for the next quarter based on customer questions.
Improve three existing pages by rewriting for clarity and checking facts.
Reach a first draft accepted with no more than one round of changes on average.

criteria.name: Clear, engaging writing
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Writes in plain words with a clear point, good structure and a voice that suits the reader.
evidence_needed: Samples have a clear main point in the first lines
levels: 0 no evidence of clear, engaging writing
1 names clear, engaging writing but gives no example
2 clear, engaging writing done with guidance or at small scale
3 clear, engaging writing done independently with a clear result
4 clear, engaging writing with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows clear, engaging writing with real examples

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?

deal_breakers.description: Admits copying text without credit or inventing quotes or facts.
deal_breakers.job_related_reason: Plagiarism and invented facts create legal and trust risk.

work_sample.title: Write a short guide
work_sample.brief: You get a fictional customer's three real questions and a few source pages. Write a 500 to 700 word guide that answers them. List your sources and mark any fact you could not confirm.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score a clear opening, correct use of sources, helpful structure, plain words, no invented facts, and honest notes about gaps. Run it through a plagiarism check if you have one.

interview_questions.question: Show me a piece you are proud of. What did you cut from the first draft and why?
good_answer_signs: Can name specific cuts and the reader reason

interview_questions.question: Tell me about a time you found a mistake in something you had published. What did you do?
How do you use AI tools in your writing? Where do you not use them?
good_answer_signs: Uses them for outlines and checks, verifies facts
weak_answer_signs: Says they do not use any tool but cannot explain why

red_flags: Samples that read the same as other web text
Cannot name a source for any fact
Only past work is unnamed or uncheckable
Samples with errors that change meaning
pay_research_hint: Compare freelance per word or per piece rates and salaried postings for writers in your region from public postings and a published pay survey.
automation_note: AI can draft outlines, summarize sources and suggest edits. A person owns the facts, the voice and the final text, and the byline.
